Number of odontogenic neoplasms cases Total no. of all cases Secondary outcome Prevalence of odontogenic neoplasms in relation to:  Age (all ages)  Gender (male &female).  Site affection. --- Research Question:  What is the prevalence of odontogenic neoplasms in educational hospitals and institutions in Cairo? Objective  The objective of this study is to determine the prevalence of odontogenic neoplams diagnosed histopathologically over a period of 5 years (from 2014 to 2018) in Cairo's educational hospitals and institutions. Furthermore, stratification of age, gender and site affection of each individual lesion will be performed.

steps.instruction: 6 D) Study size 14. Study size No sample size could be applied on our epidemiological study. E) Statistical methods 15. Statistical methods Categorical variables will be expressed in proportions or percentages; Chi square and Fisher’s exact tests will be applied as appropriate. Continuous variables will be examined for normality using Kolmogrov-Smirnov test and Shapiro-Wilk test. They will be expressed using range, mean, median± standard deviation (normal variables); range, median and interquartile range (non -normal variables). Test of significance will be used for comparison/association. The results were considered statistically significant for a value of p≤0.05.

description: 2 II. Introduction: 6a. Odontogenic tumors (OTs) comprise a complex group of lesions with diverse clinical behaviors and histological types. Some of these lesions are true neoplasms while others may represent malformations similar to tumors ( hamartomas) (Luppi et al. , 2018). Odontogenic tumors are relatively rare lesions, accounting for about 2% of all maxillofacial clinicopathological specimens sent for diagnosis to pathology services (Rubini et al., 2017). The knowledge of the epidemiological characteristics such as anatomic location, age, and gender of the patients with odontogenic tumors is extremely valuable in the development of differential diagnoses (Luppi et al. , 2018). Since a number of tumours of the jaws share the same clinical and radiographic features, (Jones et al., 2006) the diagnosis of odontogenic tumours ordinarily requires a detailed analysis of clinical, radiographical, and histopathological findings (Johnson et al., 2014) . Despite some sampling bias, diagnostic services presently, are the most reliable source of information regarding the relative frequency and clinicopathologic features of odontogenic tumours (Shekar et al., 2014). Epidemiological studies are crucial because they allow us to establish more precisely the occurrence of OTs in different populations, which in turn helps in making of a provisional diagnosis and further planning of the biopsy based on the clinical and radiographic features. It also aids in patient counseling and scheduling of treatment (Sekerci et al., 2015). A lot of the epidemiological researches relating to odontogenic tumours were conducted in other countries (Kebede et al., 2017; Silva et al., 2017; Suhasini Palakshappa et al., 2017) , despite the large number of studies on Odontogenic cysts, studies on OT are relatively rare (Soluk-Tekkeşin and Wright, 2017).
